result.title: VisCurate: Evaluating Behavioral Equivalence of Visual Skills
result.comment: Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027), Main Conference
result.summary: Modern vision-based agents have shifted toward skill-based problem-solving, where a skill is an executable image-to-image operation, e.g., cropping, thresholding, or edge detection. As these skill libraries grow, they accumulate duplicated, mislabeled, and defective skills. The signals normally used to curate them (a skill's name, description, or source code) say little about how the skill visually changes the image. We present VisCurate, a framework and benchmark that curates visual skill libraries from observed execution rather than from text. VisCurate runs each candidate skill pair on a shared probe battery and assigns one of six behavioral relations, each tied to a library edit that is safe to make. The benchmark injects seven defect types into a clean library at controlled rates, producing 300 reproducible instances with ground-truth relations and repairs. While text baselines accept up to five of six false merges on hard negatives, our verifier accepts none and recovers 51.2% of the pairs that are truly mergeable. On two real, uncurated libraries, VisCurate finds that 92% of the skills a package shares with its downstream copy are redundant, while execution confirms only 10 of 17 published equivalence claims. The curation problem also remains open, as the strongest of the nine automated curators recovers only about half of the repairs. We emphasize that visual skill libraries should be curated by behavior, not by description.

AI.brief_summary: VisCurate 提出按实际执行行为而非名称或描述来整理视觉技能库的框架与基准：在同一探针组上运行技能对，判定六种行为关系并对应安全的库编辑，同时注入七类缺陷构造可复现实例，并报告文本基线易误合并、真实库中存在大量冗余。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“用执行探针判定视觉操作功能等价”的思路，可能可供核查 VLM 推理中视觉证据是否真正影响输出、以及视觉工具集去冗余，需核查探针设计与 verifier 能否迁移到 latent 状态层面。
